title: Metabolic Flux Analysis of Flavonoid Biosynthesis (KEGG sly00941) under Osmotic and Thermal Stress
description: Doctoral research modeling carbon flux distribution through the KEGG Flavonoid Pathway (sly00941), Naringenin 3-dioxygenase (EC 1.14.11.9), and flavonol synthase under abiotic stress.
image_caption: High-Performance Liquid Chromatography (HPLC) chromatogram of quercetin and kaempferol glycosides.
overview: Flavonoids (quercetin, kaempferol, and rutin) represent powerful polyphenolic antioxidants in horticultural crops. Utilizing kinetic rate equations from the KEGG Flavonoid Biosynthesis Pathway (sly00941), this doctoral paper quantifies carbon partition coefficients between primary carbohydrate growth and secondary phenylpropanoid accumulation. Combining mild osmotic stress (drain EC 4.0 mS/cm) with a day/night temperature DIF of +6.0°C increases metabolic flux through Flavonol Synthase (EC 1.14.20.6) by +210%, doubling quercetin-3-O-rutinoside concentration in tomato skin.

climate_strategy.strategy: Apply late-stage thermal-osmotic steering: 14 days pre-harvest, elevate day temperature to 27.0°C and lower night temperature to 20.0°C (DIF +7.0°C) while maintaining substrate EC at 3.8 mS/cm.
